sources.entry: GokuRakuJoudo - Karabiner-Elements configuration manager, rescue to bloated karabiner.json

summary.one_liner: GokuRakuJoudo (Goku) is a tool that lets you write Karabiner-Elements keyboard configurations in the compact EDN format and compiles them into the verbose karabiner.json file.
summary.what_it_does: Goku reads a karabiner.edn file and generates the karabiner.json that Karabiner-Elements uses, so users can edit short EDN rules instead of thousands of lines of JSON. The `goku` command rebuilds karabiner.json once, while `gokuw` watches the EDN file and regenerates the JSON on every change. Goku can run as a background service through `brew services start goku`, with logs written to ~/Library/Logs/goku.log. The config path can be set with the GOKU_EDN_CONFIG_FILE environment variable, and a profile name can be set with the `:profiles` keyword (default is "Default"). The README also mentions using joker to lint the EDN file and watchexec to watch it.
use_cases: Editing Karabiner-Elements key remapping rules in a compact format
Mapping Caps Lock to Escape or other keys on macOS
Running a keymap compiler as a macOS background service
how_to_run: Create ~/.config/karabiner.edn (start from example.edn in the repo)
Make sure Karabiner's GUI has a profile named "Default" (or set :profiles)
notable: Converts short EDN rules into Karabiner-Elements karabiner.json
Watch mode (gokuw) regenerates config on each save
Can run as a brew background service with logs
caveats: Requires Karabiner-Elements and a profile named "Default" unless overridden
Development build requires Leiningen and, for the native binary, GraalVM native-image
Commenting out rules with #_ leaves a null rule in karabiner.json (README notes this as a known quirk, though it does not cause errors)
